text: Self-RAG retrieves passages only when needed. Special reflection tokens let the model decide whether to retrieve, critique passage relevance, and critique its own generated answer.
Self-RAG is evaluated on PubHealth, PopQA, and TriviaQA to measure factuality and open-domain question answering.

CRAG, or Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation, uses a lightweight retrieval evaluator to score retrieved documents and performs corrective retrieval when evidence is low quality. The central difference is that Self-RAG uses reflection tokens during generation, whereas CRAG explicitly evaluates retrieved documents before correction.
Toolformer trains a language model to decide when and how to call external tools by learning from self-supervised API-call annotations.
RAPTOR recursively embeds, clusters, and summarizes text chunks into a tree so retrieval can select information at several abstraction levels.
Dense Passage Retrieval, abbreviated DPR, learns separate dense encoders for questions and passages and retrieves passages with maximum inner-product search.
The method-dataset relation and its related entities are explicit: DPR evaluates open-domain question answering retrieval on Natural Questions, also called NQ, and reports top-k retrieval accuracy.
